description: Synthetic, deterministic. The /settings page has an 'Email notifications' checkbox, a 'Reset preferences' button and a status region. Reset builds a new checkbox element (document.createElement) and replaces the original with it, then shows 'Preferences reset'; no timers or requests. The test takes an ElementHandle for the checkbox before the reset, waits for the status, then calls check() on that handle, which still points to the removed node: Playwright fails at once with 'elementHandle.check: Element is not attached to the DOM' (about 0.3 s, no timeout, no retry of the handle). The app behaves as designed. A control that keeps a Locator instead resolves the replacement checkbox and passes against the same app. failureType incorrect_locator is the closest existing type: the selector is correct and resolves to the replacement; the defect is holding a one-time element reference across a DOM replacement. That the node was replaced (rather than removed) is an inference from the detached error together with error-context, which shows a checkbox with the same name and the 'Preferences reset' status; no tool exposes DOM node identity. Neither get_trace_summary nor the screenshot is required.

tests.title: enables email notifications after resetting preferences

rootCause.summary: The test keeps an ElementHandle taken before the reset; the reset replaces the checkbox with a new node, so check() on the old handle fails because that node is no longer attached to the DOM.
